title: Jira vs Plane
comparison_markdown:
# Jira vs Plane (2026)

## Overview
Jira and Plane are two project management tools that help teams organize and track their work. This comparison is useful for teams currently using Jira who are considering switching to Plane, possibly due to the desire for more control over their data or a self-hosted solution. The core use case for both tools is issue tracking and project management, and someone would switch if they need more flexibility or a free, self-hosted option.

## Key Differences
* Cost: Jira is a paid service, while Plane is free and self-hosted.
* Data ownership: Plane allows users to have full control over their data, while Jira stores data on its servers.
* Setup complexity: Plane requires more technical expertise to set up, while Jira is generally easier to get started with.
* Scalability: Jira is designed to handle large, complex projects, while Plane is better suited for smaller to medium-sized teams.
* Integration with Git: Jira has native integration with Git, while Plane uses a third-party plugin for Git integration.

## Pricing Comparison
| Aspect | Jira | Plane |
|--------|----------|---------|
| Base Cost | $7.75-$14.50/user/month | Free (self-hosted) |
| License | Proprietary | Apache 2.0 |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Per-user cost at 50 users | $387.50-$725/month | $0 (server cost only) |
| Per-user cost at 200 users | $1,550-$2,900/month | $0 (server cost only) |

## Pros and Cons
### Jira
* Pros:
  + Easy to use and set up
  + Robust feature set
  + Good customer support
  + Integrates well with other Atlassian tools
  + Scalable
* Cons:
  + Expensive, especially for large teams
  + Data stored on Jira's servers
  + Limited customization options
  + Can be overwhelming for small teams
  + Not self-hosted
### Plane
* Pros:
  + Free and self-hosted
  + Full control over data
  + Customizable
  + Cost-effective
  + Open-source
* Cons:
  + More complex to set up
  + Limited customer support
  + Not as scalable as Jira
  + Limited integrations with other tools
  + Requires technical expertise

## When to Choose Each
Jira is a good choice for large, complex teams that need a robust feature set and are willing to pay for it. It's also a good option for teams that are already invested in the Atlassian ecosystem. On the other hand, Plane is a good choice for smaller teams or teams on a budget that want a self-hosted solution and are willing to handle the technical complexity. It's also a good option for teams that value data ownership and customization.

## Migration Path
1. Export your Jira data in CSV or JSON format.
2. Use a third-party import tool, such as the Plane importer, to import your data into Plane.
3. Configure your Plane instance to match your Jira setup, including setting up users, projects, and workflows.
4. Test your Plane instance to ensure everything is working as expected.
5. Switch your team over to Plane and provide training on the new system.

## Our Take
Plane is not yet production-ready for most users, as it still lacks some of the features and polish of Jira. One specific technical limitation worth knowing is that Plane's scalability is limited compared to Jira, so large teams may find it difficult to use. However, for small to medium-sized teams that value data ownership and customization, Plane is a good option, and we recommend switching from Jira to Plane if you don't need the advanced features and scalability of Jira.

## Who Should Switch
* Small teams (less than 10 users) that don't need advanced features
* Teams on a budget that want a free, self-hosted solution
* Teams that value data ownership and customization
* Teams with simple project management needs
* Teams with technical expertise that can handle the complexity of Plane

## FAQ
### Can I use Plane for large, complex projects?
No, Plane is not yet suitable for large, complex projects due to its limited scalability.
### Is Plane free?
Yes, Plane is free and self-hosted.
### Can I integrate Plane with other tools?
Yes, Plane can be integrated with other tools using third-party plugins, but the options are limited compared to Jira.
### How do I migrate from Jira to Plane?
You can migrate from Jira to Plane by exporting your Jira data and using a third-party import tool to import it into Plane.
### Is Plane open-source?
Yes, Plane is open-source and uses the Apache 2.0 license.

title: Trello vs WeKan
comparison_markdown:
# Trello vs WeKan

## Overview

Trello is a visual kanban board tool from Atlassian, simple and beginner-friendly. WeKan is an open-source kanban board offering the same card/list/board model without vendor dependency.

## Key Differences

- **Cost**: Trello paid plans start at $5/user/month; WeKan is completely free
- **Data control**: WeKan runs on your own server; Trello data lives on Atlassian infrastructure
- **Features**: Trello has a larger Power-Ups marketplace; WeKan covers core kanban features
- **Setup**: Trello requires zero setup; WeKan requires a server
- **Customization**: WeKan open-source code can be extended; Trello cannot

## Pricing Comparison

| Aspect | Trello | WeKan |
|--------|-------------------------------|-------------------------------|
| Base pricing | Free / $5+/user/month | Free (self-hosted) |
| License | Proprietary | MIT |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Cost at 50 users | See pricing page | $0/month (self-hosted) |
| Cost at 200 users | See pricing page | $0/month (self-hosted) |
| Vendor lock-in | High | None |

## Pros and Cons

### Trello

**Pros:**
- Polished, professionally designed user interface
- Large ecosystem of official integrations
- Managed infrastructure with no server maintenance required
- Enterprise SLA and dedicated support available
- Mobile apps are well-maintained and reliable

**Cons:**
- Significant per-user monthly cost that scales linearly with team size
- Your data is stored on the vendor infrastructure
- No ability to inspect or modify the source code
- Feature roadmap controlled entirely by the vendor
- Risk of pricing changes, acquisition, or discontinuation

### WeKan

**Pros:**
- Free to self-host with costs only for server infrastructure
- Complete data ownership and privacy control
- Source code is auditable and modifiable
- Active open-source community
- No vendor lock-in or risk of sudden pricing changes
> GitHub: [wekan/wekan](https://github.com/wekan/wekan) * ~20k stars

**Cons:**
- Requires technical knowledge to self-host and maintain
- May lack some advanced features found in the proprietary version
- Support relies on community forums rather than a paid helpdesk
- UI polish may lag behind the proprietary tool
- You are responsible for updates, backups, and security patches

## When to Choose Each

**Choose Trello if:** Trello suits individuals and small teams wanting instant zero-setup kanban with integrations to Slack, Google Drive, and GitHub.

**Choose WeKan if:** WeKan is ideal for teams wanting full data ownership or air-gapped deployments.

## Migration Path

Export Trello boards as JSON, then use WeKan Trello importer in Settings to recreate boards, lists, and cards.

## Our Take

WeKan is production-ready for most teams willing to invest a few hours in setup. The self-hosted version gives you identical or better functionality to the paid Trello tiers, with no recurring per-seat cost.

The main technical limitation worth knowing: you are responsible for your own backups, updates, and uptime. If your server goes down, so does your WeKan instance. Plan for this with automated backups and a monitoring alert.

Our recommendation: if your team has at least one developer and you are paying more than $100/month for Trello, switching to self-hosted WeKan will pay for itself within the first month. If nobody on your team is comfortable with Linux or Docker, stay on Trello until you have that resource.

## Who Should Switch

- Startups under 20 people paying per-seat fees they cannot yet justify
- Dev teams who already self-host other tools and have the ops knowledge
- Organizations in jurisdictions with strict data residency requirements
- Teams who have evaluated Trello paid features and only use the basics
- Founders and solopreneurs who want the functionality without the subscription

## FAQ

### Is WeKan free to use?
Yes. WeKan is free to self-host. Your only cost is the server, typically $6-$12/month on a VPS provider like DigitalOcean or Vultr.

### How hard is it to migrate from Trello to WeKan?
For most teams, migration takes 2-4 hours. Export your Trello data, follow the WeKan import guide, and test with a small group before switching everyone over.

### Does WeKan get regular updates?
Yes. WeKan has an active open-source community with regular releases. Check the GitHub repository for release frequency.

### Can I use WeKan without technical knowledge?
You need basic comfort with a VPS and command line. If that feels unfamiliar, there are managed hosting options that handle the server for you at a modest cost.

### What happens if WeKan development stops?
Because the source code is open, you can continue running whatever version you have indefinitely. You can also fork the project or switch to another tool at your own pace — no vendor can shut off your instance.

---
*Data sourced July 2026. Pricing and features change. Verify at [Trello](https://trello.com) and [WeKan](https://wekan.github.io) before making decisions.*

You need basic comfort with a VPS and command line. If that feels unfamiliar, there are managed hosting options that handle the server for you at a modest cost.

title: Linear vs Plane

# Linear vs Plane (2026)

## Overview
Linear and Plane are two project management tools that help teams organize and track their work. This comparison is beneficial for teams currently using Linear who are considering switching to Plane, possibly due to Plane's self-hosted option and free cost. The core use case for both tools is project management, and the key reason someone would switch is to gain more control over their data and reduce costs.

## Key Differences
* Cost: Linear charges $8 per user per month, while Plane is free and self-hosted.
* Data ownership: Plane allows teams to have full control over their data, while Linear stores data on its servers.
* Setup complexity: Linear is generally easier to set up, while Plane requires more technical expertise to self-host.
* Scalability: Plane is highly scalable, but requires more maintenance and upkeep, while Linear handles scalability automatically.
* Integration with GitHub: Linear has a more seamless integration with GitHub, while Plane's integration is still in development.

## Pricing Comparison
| Aspect | Linear | Plane |
|--------|----------|---------|
| Base Cost | Free / $8/user/month | Free (self-hosted) |
| License | Proprietary | Apache 2.0 |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Per-user cost at 50 users | $400/month | $0 (server cost only) |
| Per-user cost at 200 users | $1,600/month | $0 (server cost only) |

## Pros and Cons
**Linear:**
* Easy to set up and use
* Seamless integration with GitHub
* Automatic scalability
* Good customer support
* Limited control over data
**Plane:**
* Free and self-hosted
* Full control over data
* Highly scalable
* Customizable
* Steeper learning curve

## When to Choose Each
Linear is a good choice for small to medium-sized teams who need a simple and easy-to-use project management tool. It's also a good choice for teams who don't require full control over their data and are willing to pay a monthly fee per user. Plane, on the other hand, is a good choice for larger teams or teams with complex project management needs who require full control over their data and are willing to invest time and resources into self-hosting and maintenance.

## Migration Path
1. Export data from Linear in CSV or JSON format.
2. Set up a Plane server and configure it to meet your team's needs.
3. Use the Plane import tool to import your data from Linear.
4. Test and verify that all data has been imported correctly.
5. Update any integrations or workflows to point to the new Plane server.

## Our Take
Plane is not yet production-ready for most users, as it still lacks some features and polish. One specific technical limitation worth knowing is that Plane's integration with GitHub is still in development and may not be as seamless as Linear's. However, for teams who require full control over their data and are willing to invest time and resources into self-hosting and maintenance, Plane is a good choice.

## Who Should Switch
* Small teams (less than 10 users) who don't need GitHub integration
* Teams with simple project management needs who want to save on costs
* Teams who require full control over their data and are willing to self-host
* Large teams (over 100 users) who want to reduce their monthly costs
* Teams who don't need automatic scalability and are willing to handle it themselves

## FAQ
### Is Plane free?
Yes, Plane is free and self-hosted.
### Can I self-host Linear?
No, Linear is not available for self-hosting.
### Is Plane's integration with GitHub seamless?
Not yet, Plane's integration with GitHub is still in development.
### Can I export my data from Linear?
Yes, you can export your data from Linear in CSV or JSON format.
### Is Plane suitable for small teams?
Yes, Plane can be suitable for small teams who don't need GitHub integration and want to save on costs.

* Scalability: Google Workspace is highly scalable, while Nextcloud's scalability depends on the hosting infrastructure.
* Integration: Google Workspace has native integration with Google Drive, while Nextcloud has integration with OnlyOffice for document editing.

| Aspect | Google Workspace | Nextcloud |
|--------|----------|---------|
| Base Cost | $6-$18/user/month | Free (self-hosted) |
